title: How I keep leads coming when the phone goes quiet
summary: Wave season ends, the phone goes quiet, and the pipeline still has to move. Here's how a cruise agent fills the next busy season.
body_markdown:
My first year as a travel agent, bookings poured in during the stretch from January through March. That’s what we call wave season in the cruise industry, when people get past the labyrinth of the holidays and plan their year ahead. Then the rush ended, and my phone went quiet. I spent those weeks sitting on my hands, worrying. Other agents reassured me that business comes and goes, but until you’ve lived through it, you don’t really trust that.


I run Intermission Travel, a one-person agency just outside Atlanta. Cruises are 80 to 85% of my business.


Part of what made that first quiet stretch so nerve-racking is I don’t get paid when a client books. I get paid once they pass final payment, three to four months before sailing, or after the trip. A cruise I book a year and a half out pays me nothing for a long while. So my pipeline’s got to be continually moving.


Over time, I figured out how to use the slow months. I study new products and turn what I learn into social content. I catch up on admin, too, and sell add-ons like insurance and excursions on trips that are already booked. It’s another way to juice up otherwise slow sales.


Quo works as a mini CRM for me. After[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) for lead capture finishes an intake, I paste the details into the contact’s notes, so I know what every lead asked about. Some leads are what I call tire kickers: they get a quote, say thanks, and roll on. Then a cruise line runs a promotion that fits them, and I want to be the first guy in their inbox.


Right now, 10,000 Black Friday cruise deals are landing at once. I had ChatGPT help me grade them, and I send a newsletter every other day to sort them out. It serves a need, but it also collects emails and phone numbers. One subscriber who never uses travel agents asked about an Alaska cruise tour, one of the most confusing things in travel to buy. I built a seven-question interactive site that ends in a real price. The subscriber wrote back: “Anybody who puts that much into answering one simple question deserves my business. When do we talk?”


Wherever people find me, the call to action is the same: text me. My[TikTok handle](https://www.tiktok.com/@intermissiontravel) and profile picture are both my phone number, and my link in bio goes straight to Quo.


If someone doesn’t hear back within two hours, they’ll move on, because they can book with the cruise line instantly. I used to have a one-line auto-reply saying I’d get to them soon. Now Sona answers right away. It handles the basic questions I’ve got to ask everyone, like sail dates, budget, and cabin type, then takes a name and email. A fast reply makes me look bigger than I am and like I’ve got a receptionist. In a way I do.


When I follow up, I’ve already read the brief, and the client feels heard. By the time their credit card comes out, I’ve stepped in. Sona saves me at least five hours a week.


One client, who works in credit card technology, watched Sona hand her over to me mid-conversation. I was working on something else, half-watching Sona handle her intake, when I saw it catch a detail I hadn’t told it: she wanted the same cruise another client had booked, but a different cabin. By the time Sona wrapped up, I texted: “Hey, this is Jon jumping in.” She called it the smoothest AI experience she’d ever seen.


That first year I was in business, I waited for the phone to ring. Now the quiet months are when I fill the next busy season. I grade deals, build things like the Alaska site, and go back to the leads who weren’t ready yet. There’s no way you can ever learn everything in this industry. There’s something changing all the time.


##


Three things to try this week


---


1. **Log what each lead asks about.** After Sona finishes an intake, copy the summary into the contact’s notes in Quo. When a promotion lands, search a word like “Hawaii” or “Alaska” and message the people it fits.
2. **Put your number where people already look.** Make your phone number your[social handle](https://www.tiktok.com/@intermissiontravel) , point your bio links to a Quo number, and end every post with “text me.” That’s what I do.
3. **Have Sona ask the first questions.** Set it up to collect what you’d ask every new lead anyway. For me, that’s sail date, budget, party size, cabin type, name, and email. Then, you step in having already read the brief.


##


Let Sona answer the phones while you’re away


**Justine Delgadillo**
Sr. Customer Solutions & Education Manager, Quo


---


It’s 11:48 p.m. on Christmas Eve, and a customer calls to ask whether you’re open on January 1. You’re asleep, which is the point of the break.[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) isn’t. It can answer that question, share your holiday hours and shipping deadlines, and take a message when it doesn’t know the answer.


### How to set up Sona before a holiday break


1. In the call flow builder on desktop, click + **Create new call flow** and give it a name, such as “Holiday hours.” This keeps your default flow untouched.
2. Drag a **Sona** step in right after the incoming call, so Sona answers every caller.
3. Edit the greeting. Include your business name, a line saying Sona is an AI assistant, a recording notice, and your closure dates.


For example:


*Hi there, this is Sona, an AI assistant for \[business\]. We’re closed from \[date\] to \[date\], but I can answer questions or take a message. Please note this call is being recorded.*


1. Click **Add knowledge** and paste in your holiday hours, closure dates, shipping deadlines, return policy, and FAQs. You can also add a page URL or upload a file (PDF, CSV, Markdown, JSON, or plain text, up to 10 MB). Each page maxes out at 20,000 characters.
2. Click **Add job** and start from the message-taking template. Tell Sona to collect the caller’s name, number, and reason for calling.
3. Click **Test Sona** , place a mock call, and ask the holiday-hours question yourself.
4. Click the arrow next to **Publish now** , choose **Schedule to publish later** , and pick the start date and time. Then[schedule your default flow](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/call-flows/temp-call-flows) to resume. Skip that step and the holiday flow keeps running.
5. When you’re back, read the AI call summaries and add anything Sona couldn’t answer to its knowledge.


Sona can also text a link mid-call, such as your FAQ page, as long as the number is registered for business messaging.
